chunks: Umar ibn Yazid asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the narration that they report: 'It is not appropriate to offer voluntary prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer.' What is the limit of this time? He said, 'When the resident begins the Iqamah.' He said to him, 'The people differ regarding the Iqamah.' He said, 'The Iqamah is that by which you pray with them.'

key_terms.الْإِقَامَة: the second call to prayer, signaling the immediate start of the congregational prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time for prohibited voluntary prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Umar ibn Yazid seeks to resolve the scholarly dispute regarding the precise onset of the 'time of fard' prayer where voluntary (nafl) prayers are prohibited. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical, communal definition—stating that the time begins when the Iqamah is recited for the congregational prayer—thereby anchoring the legal ruling in the observable practice of the community rather than abstract astronomical calculations. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the Iqamah as the definitive marker for the transition from individual preparation to communal obligation.
